title: Maximum Equal Frequency
summary: Given an array of positive integers, find the longest prefix such that by removing exactly one element, all numbers in the prefix will have the same frequency of occurrence.
statement: Given an array of positive integers, find the longest prefix such that by removing exactly one element, all numbers in the prefix will have the same frequency of occurrence. If removing one element results in an empty prefix, consider that all numbers have a frequency of zero.
constraints: Choose the longest prefix from which deleting exactly one element leaves all remaining value frequencies equal.
The remaining prefix may be empty.
reference_solution:
def maximum_equal_frequency_prefix(nums):
    counts=Counter();frequencies=Counter();maximum=answer=0
    for index,value in enumerate(nums,1):
        old=counts[value]
        if old:frequencies[old]-=1
        counts[value]+=1;frequencies[old+1]+=1;maximum=max(maximum,old+1)
        if maximum==1 or maximum*frequencies[maximum]+1==index or (maximum-1)*(frequencies[maximum-1]+1)+1==index:answer=index
    return answer

hints: Maintain value counts and how many values have each count.
A prefix is valid when all counts are one, one value occurs once, or one value has frequency exactly one above all others.
Test those arithmetic identities after each insertion.
These are the only ways one deletion can make every positive frequency equal.
